source.text: וַיֵּשְׁב֥וּ שָׂרֵֽי־הָעָ֖ם בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וּשְׁאָ֣ר הָ֠עָם הִפִּ֨ילוּ גוֹרָל֜וֹת לְהָבִ֣יא׀אֶחָ֣ד מִן־הָעֲשָׂרָ֗ה לָשֶׁ֨בֶת֙ בִּֽירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ עִ֣יר הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ וְתֵ֥שַׁע הַיָּד֖וֹת בֶּעָרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And dwelt [the] princes of the people in Jerusalem; and [the] rest of the people cast lots to bring one of the ten to dwell in Jerusalem, the city of the holiness, and nine of the hands in the cities.

en.L: And the princes of the people lived in Jerusalem; and the rest of the people cast lots to bring one of ten to live in Jerusalem, the holy city, and nine parts [stayed] in the [other] towns.
en.B: The officials of the people settled in Jerusalem. The rest of the people cast lots to bring one out of every ten to live in Jerusalem, the holy city, while the other nine stayed in the other towns.
en.R: The leaders of the people lived in Jerusalem. The rest of the people threw lots to choose one person out of every ten to live in Jerusalem, the holy city. The other nine out of ten stayed in their own towns.

decisions.choice: settling Jerusalem: filling the rebuilt city with people
decisions.reason: When the wall was finished, the city was large but there were few people in it and the houses had not been rebuilt (7:4). This chapter tells how it was filled, picking up the story where 7:4-5 left it.

decisions.choice: one of ten by lot: a tenth of the people chosen to move to the city
decisions.reason: The lot left the choice to God (10:35; Proverbs 16:33). A tenth of the people would leave their towns and fields to live in the capital.

decisions.choice: the holy city: Jerusalem, as the place of God's house
decisions.reason: Nehemiah 11:1 and 11:18 are the first places in the Bible where Jerusalem is called "the holy city"; Isaiah 48:2 and 52:1 also use the name. The city is holy because the house of God stands in it.

decisions.choice: nine of the hands: nine parts out of ten
decisions.reason: "Hand" can mean a share or part (Genesis 43:34; 47:24). Nine parts of the people stayed where they were.

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); officials (Balanced); leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: The project's usual wording for this title of rank. Balanced and Readable add "other", and Readable "their own", since the towns are those outside Jerusalem.

source.text: וַֽיְבָרֲכ֖וּ הָעָ֑ם לְכֹל֙ הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים הַמִּֽתְנַדְּבִ֔ים לָשֶׁ֖בֶת בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And blessed the people all the men volunteering to dwell in Jerusalem.

en.L: And the people blessed all the men who volunteered to live in Jerusalem.
en.B: The people blessed all the men who volunteered to live in Jerusalem.
en.R: The people asked God to bless all the men who offered to live in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: volunteered: offered themselves willingly
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for freewill offerings and for willing service (Judges 5:2, 9; Ezra 1:6; 2:68). Moving to the city meant leaving one's land and living where there was little to live on and danger was near, so the willingness was praised.

decisions.choice: the volunteers: either men besides those chosen by lot, or those chosen who went willingly
alternatives: men who volunteered in addition to the tenth chosen by lot
decisions.reason: The verse does not say how the volunteers relate to the lot of verse 1. They may have been men who offered to go besides those the lot chose, or the people may have praised those chosen for accepting it gladly.

decisions.choice: asked God to bless
decisions.reason: To bless someone is to speak good over them and ask God's good for them; Readable says so.

source.text: וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ רָאשֵׁ֣י הַמְּדִינָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָשְׁב֖וּ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וּבְעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה יָֽשְׁב֞וּ אִ֤ישׁ בַּאֲחֻזָּתוֹ֙ בְּעָ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל הַכֹּהֲנִים֙ וְהַלְוִיִּ֣ם וְהַנְּתִינִ֔ים וּבְנֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֥י שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And these [are the] heads of the province who dwelt in Jerusalem; and in [the] cities of Judah dwelt, each in his property in their cities, Israel, the priests and the Levites and the Nethinim and [the] sons of [the] slaves of Solomon.

en.L: And these [are] the heads of the province who lived in Jerusalem; and in the towns of Judah lived, each on his property in their towns, Israel, the priests and the Levites and the Nethinim and the sons of the slaves of Solomon.
en.B: These are the leaders of the province who lived in Jerusalem. In the towns of Judah lived the Israelites, the priests, the Levites, the temple servants and the descendants of Solomon's servants, every family on its own property in their towns.
en.R: Here are the leaders of the province who lived in Jerusalem. The other Israelites, priests, Levites, temple servants and descendants of Solomon's servants lived in the towns of Judah, every family on its own land.

decisions.choice: the province: the Persian province of Judah
decisions.reason: The word names a district of the Persian empire (1:3; 7:6; Ezra 2:1). Judah was a small province with Jerusalem as its center.

decisions.choice: the towns of Judah: a word in passing about those who did not move
decisions.reason: The verse names the list that follows (verses 4-24, those in Jerusalem) and adds that the rest lived in the towns. The towns themselves are listed in verses 25-36.

decisions.choice: the list of Jerusalem's residents: a similar list in 1 Chronicles 9
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 9:2-34 gives a list of those who lived in Jerusalem after the exile with many of the same names and families, though with differences in names and numbers.

decisions.choice: Israel, the priests, the Levites, the Nethinim, the descendants of Solomon's servants: the groups of the community
decisions.reason: "Israel" here means the lay people, as distinct from the priests and Levites (Ezra 10:25). The temple servants and the descendants of Solomon's servants were families attached to the temple's service (7:46-60; Ezra 2:43-58).

decisions.choice: each on his property (Literal), every family on its own property (Balanced, Readable); the Nethinim, the sons of the slaves of Solomon (Literal), the temple servants, the descendants of Solomon's servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The property was held by families, so Balanced and Readable say "every family". The names of the temple groups follow the project's wording for Ezra and Nehemiah.

source.text: וּבִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ יָֽשְׁב֔וּ מִבְּנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה וּמִבְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ן מִבְּנֵ֣י יְ֠הוּדָה עֲתָיָ֨ה בֶן־עֻזִּיָּ֜ה בֶּן־זְכַרְיָ֧ה בֶן־אֲמַרְיָ֛ה בֶּן־שְׁפַטְיָ֥ה בֶן־מַהֲלַלְאֵ֖ל מִבְּנֵי־פָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And in Jerusalem dwelt [some] of [the] sons of Judah and [some] of [the] sons of Benjamin. Of [the] sons of Judah: Athaiah son of Uzziah, son of Zechariah, son of Amariah, son of Shephatiah, son of Mahalalel, of [the] sons of Perez;

en.L: And in Jerusalem lived some of the sons of Judah and some of the sons of Benjamin. Of the sons of Judah: Athaiah son of Uzziah, son of Zechariah, son of Amariah, son of Shephatiah, son of Mahalalel, of the sons of Perez;
en.B: Some of the descendants of Judah and some of the descendants of Benjamin lived in Jerusalem. From the descendants of Judah: Athaiah son of Uzziah, son of Zechariah, son of Amariah, son of Shephatiah, son of Mahalalel, a descendant of Perez;
en.R: Some of the descendants of Judah and of Benjamin lived in Jerusalem. From the descendants of Judah there was Athaiah son of Uzziah, the son of Zechariah, the son of Amariah, the son of Shephatiah, the son of Mahalalel, from the family of Perez.

decisions.choice: Judah and Benjamin: the two tribes whose land lay around Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Jerusalem stood on the border of Judah and Benjamin (Joshua 15:8; 18:16), and most of the exiles who came back were from these two tribes (Ezra 1:5).

decisions.choice: son of ... son of: a line of ancestors, not always complete
decisions.reason: Such lists trace a man back through his forefathers to show his family's standing. They often leave out generations, naming the important ones.

decisions.choice: Perez: son of Judah, ancestor of David
decisions.reason: Perez was the son of Judah and Tamar (Genesis 38:29). His line was the leading clan of Judah and led to David (Ruth 4:18-22).

source.text: וּמַעֲשֵׂיָ֣ה בֶן־בָּר֣וּךְ בֶּן־כָּל־חֹ֠זֶה בֶּן־חֲזָיָ֨ה בֶן־עֲדָיָ֧ה בֶן־יוֹיָרִ֛יב בֶּן־זְכַרְיָ֖ה בֶּן־הַשִּׁלֹנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: and Maaseiah son of Baruch, son of Col-Hozeh, son of Hazaiah, son of Adaiah, son of Joiarib, son of Zechariah, son of the Shilonite.

en.L: and Maaseiah son of Baruch, son of Col-Hozeh, son of Hazaiah, son of Adaiah, son of Joiarib, son of Zechariah, son of the Shilonite.
en.B: and Maaseiah son of Baruch, son of Col-Hozeh, son of Hazaiah, son of Adaiah, son of Joiarib, son of Zechariah, a descendant of the Shilonite.
en.R: There was also Maaseiah son of Baruch, the son of Col-Hozeh, the son of Hazaiah, the son of Adaiah, the son of Joiarib, the son of Zechariah, from the family of the Shilonite.

decisions.choice: the Shilonite: probably a descendant of Shelah son of Judah
decisions.reason: Maaseiah belongs to Judah, and the families of Judah were Perez, Zerah and Shelah (Numbers 26:20, where the Shelanites are named). With slightly different vowels the same letters would mean "of Shelah". The same letters could also mean a man from the town of Shiloh, as Ahijah the Shilonite was (1 Kings 11:29), but Shiloh lay in Ephraim.

decisions.choice: Col-Hozeh: a family known from the building of the wall
decisions.reason: Shallun son of Col-Hozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired the Fountain Gate (3:15).

source.text: כָּל־בְּנֵי־פֶ֕רֶץ הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם אַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֛וֹת שִׁשִּׁ֥ים וּשְׁמֹנָ֖ה אַנְשֵׁי־חָֽיִל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: All [the] sons of Perez dwelling in Jerusalem: four hundred sixty and eight men of strength.

en.L: All the sons of Perez who lived in Jerusalem: 468 men of strength.
en.B: All the descendants of Perez who lived in Jerusalem were 468 able men.
en.R: In all, 468 strong, able men from the family of Perez lived in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: men of strength: able men, fit to serve and to defend
decisions.reason: The word for strength covers ability, wealth and military worth. In a city that needed guarding (7:3), these were men able to work and to fight.

source.text: וְאֵ֖לֶּה בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִ֑ן סַלֻּ֡א בֶּן־מְשֻׁלָּ֡ם בֶּן־יוֹעֵ֡ד בֶּן־פְּדָיָה֩ בֶן־ק֨וֹלָיָ֧ה בֶן־מַעֲשֵׂיָ֛ה בֶּן־אִֽיתִיאֵ֖ל בֶּן־יְשַֽׁעְיָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And these [are the] sons of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Joed, son of Pedaiah, son of Kolaiah, son of Maaseiah, son of Ithiel, son of Jeshaiah;

en.L: And these [are] the sons of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Joed, son of Pedaiah, son of Kolaiah, son of Maaseiah, son of Ithiel, son of Jeshaiah;
en.B: These are the descendants of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Joed, son of Pedaiah, son of Kolaiah, son of Maaseiah, son of Ithiel, son of Jeshaiah;
en.R: These are the descendants of Benjamin: Sallu son of Meshullam, the son of Joed, the son of Pedaiah, the son of Kolaiah, the son of Maaseiah, the son of Ithiel, the son of Jeshaiah.

decisions.choice: Sallu son of Meshullam: also in 1 Chronicles 9:7
decisions.reason: The list in 1 Chronicles 9:7 names "Sallu son of Meshullam" among the Benjaminites of Jerusalem, with a different line of ancestors.

source.text: וְאַחֲרָ֖יו גַּבַּ֣י סַלָּ֑י תְּשַׁ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וּשְׁמֹנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and after him Gabbai, Sallai: nine hundred twenty and eight.

en.L: and after him Gabbai, Sallai: 928.
en.B: and after him Gabbai and Sallai: 928 in all.
en.R: Next came Gabbai and Sallai. There were 928 men from Benjamin in all.

decisions.choice: after him Gabbai, Sallai: the list goes on, though the words are hard
alternatives: and his brothers, men of strength
decisions.reason: "After him" usually means "next to him" or "under him" (as in chapter 3). Two names follow and then the number for all the Benjaminites. Some think a few words were lost or changed in copying, since with small changes the letters could read "and his brothers, men of strength", like verses 6 and 14. The text as it stands is translated.

decisions.choice: in all; men from Benjamin
decisions.reason: The number is the total of the Benjaminites in the city, as verse 6 gives the total of Perez; Balanced and Readable say so.

source.text: וְיוֹאֵ֥ל בֶּן־זִכְרִ֖י פָּקִ֣יד עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וִיהוּדָ֧ה בֶן־הַסְּנוּאָ֛ה עַל־הָעִ֖יר מִשְׁנֶֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And Joel son of Zikri [was] overseer over them, and Judah son of Hassenuah over the city second.

en.L: And Joel son of Zikri [was] overseer over them, and Judah son of Hassenuah [was] over the city, second.
en.B: Joel son of Zikri was their overseer, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second in command over the city.
en.R: Joel son of Zikri was in charge of them, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second in charge of the city.

decisions.choice: over the city, second: second in command over the city
alternatives: over the second district of the city
decisions.reason: The word "second" can mean the second in rank, or the newer part of Jerusalem called the Mishneh, the second district (2 Kings 22:14; Zephaniah 1:10). The order of the words fits either reading; this translation takes the first.

decisions.choice: overseer: an officer set over a group
decisions.reason: The word is used for an appointed officer in charge of a body of people or work (verses 14, 22; Genesis 41:34).

source.text: מִן־הַֽכֹּהֲנִ֑ים יְדַֽעְיָ֥ה בֶן־יוֹיָרִ֖יב יָכִֽין׃

records.literal_gloss: Of the priests: Jedaiah son of Joiarib, Jakin,

en.L: Of the priests: Jedaiah son of Joiarib, Jakin,
en.B: From the priests: Jedaiah son of Joiarib, Jakin,
en.R: From the priests there were Jedaiah son of Joiarib, Jakin,

decisions.choice: Jedaiah son of Joiarib, Jakin: perhaps three names, "Jedaiah, Joiarib, Jakin"
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 9:10 has "Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, Jachin", three names of priestly families, all of them divisions of the priests (1 Chronicles 24:7, 17). Here the Hebrew has "son of" between the first two. The text as it stands is translated, but the word may have entered in copying.

source.text: שְׂרָיָ֨ה בֶן־חִלְקִיָּ֜ה בֶּן־מְשֻׁלָּ֣ם בֶּן־צָד֗וֹק בֶּן־מְרָיוֹת֙ בֶּן־אֲחִיט֔וּב נְגִ֖ד בֵּ֥ית הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Seraiah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, chief officer of [the] house of God,

en.L: Seraiah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, chief officer of the house of God,
en.B: Seraiah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, the chief officer of the house of God,
en.R: Seraiah son of Hilkiah, the son of Meshullam, the son of Zadok, the son of Meraioth, the son of Ahitub, the official in charge of God's temple,

decisions.choice: Seraiah's line: the family of the high priests
decisions.reason: The names Hilkiah, Shallum or Meshullam, Zadok and Ahitub are the line of the high priests before the exile (1 Chronicles 5:38-40, numbered 6:12-14 in many Bibles; Ezra 7:1-2). Seraiah is of that family; 1 Chronicles 9:11 has Azariah in his place.

decisions.choice: chief officer of the house of God: a leading officer of the temple
decisions.reason: The title means a leader or ruler. It is used of the temple's chief officers (1 Chronicles 9:11; 2 Chronicles 31:13). It may belong to Seraiah or to his ancestor Ahitub, as in 1 Chronicles 9:11.

source.text: וַאֲחֵיהֶ֗ם עֹשֵׂ֤י הַמְּלָאכָה֙ לַבַּ֔יִת שְׁמֹנֶ֥ה מֵא֖וֹת עֶשְׂרִ֣ים וּשְׁנָ֑יִם וַ֠עֲדָיָה בֶּן־יְרֹחָ֤ם בֶּן־פְּלַלְיָה֙ בֶּן־אַמְצִ֣י בֶן־זְכַרְיָ֔ה בֶּן־פַּשְׁח֖וּר בֶּן־מַלְכִּיָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and their brothers doing the work of the house: eight hundred twenty and two; and Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pelaliah, son of Amzi, son of Zechariah, son of Pashhur, son of Malkijah,

en.L: and their brothers who did the work of the house: 822; and Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pelaliah, son of Amzi, son of Zechariah, son of Pashhur, son of Malkijah,
en.B: and their fellow priests who did the work of the temple, 822 in all; and Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pelaliah, son of Amzi, son of Zechariah, son of Pashhur, son of Malkijah,
en.R: and their fellow priests who did the work in the temple, 822 in all. There was also Adaiah son of Jeroham, the son of Pelaliah, the son of Amzi, the son of Zechariah, the son of Pashhur, the son of Malkijah,

decisions.choice: their brothers: their fellow priests
decisions.reason: "Brothers" means the other members of the same group, here the priests serving under these leaders.

decisions.choice: the work of the house: the service of the temple
decisions.reason: "The house" is the house of God named in verse 11. The work is the priests' service of sacrifice and worship.

decisions.choice: fellow priests; the temple
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who the brothers are and which house is meant.

source.text: וְאֶחָיו֙ רָאשִׁ֣ים לְאָב֔וֹת מָאתַ֖יִם אַרְבָּעִ֣ים וּשְׁנָ֑יִם וַעֲמַשְׁסַ֧י בֶּן־עֲזַרְאֵ֛ל בֶּן־אַחְזַ֥י בֶּן־מְשִׁלֵּמ֖וֹת בֶּן־אִמֵּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: and his brothers, heads of fathers: two hundred forty and two; and Amashsai son of Azarel, son of Ahzai, son of Meshillemoth, son of Immer,

en.L: and his brothers, heads of fathers: 242; and Amashsai son of Azarel, son of Ahzai, son of Meshillemoth, son of Immer,
en.B: and his fellow priests, heads of families, 242 in all; and Amashsai son of Azarel, son of Ahzai, son of Meshillemoth, son of Immer,
en.R: and his fellow priests, who were family leaders, 242 in all. There was also Amashsai son of Azarel, the son of Ahzai, the son of Meshillemoth, the son of Immer,

decisions.choice: heads of fathers: heads of families
decisions.reason: Short for heads of the fathers' houses, the extended families by which the people were organized (10:35).

decisions.choice: Immer: a priestly family
decisions.reason: The descendants of Immer were one of the priestly families of the first return (7:40; Ezra 2:37), and Immer is a division of priests (1 Chronicles 24:14).

source.text: וַאֲחֵיהֶם֙ גִּבּ֣וֹרֵי חַ֔יִל מֵאָ֖ה עֶשְׂרִ֣ים וּשְׁמֹנָ֑ה וּפָקִ֣יד עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם זַבְדִּיאֵ֖ל בֶּן־הַגְּדוֹלִֽים׃ס

records.literal_gloss: and their brothers, mighty [men] of strength: one hundred twenty and eight; and overseer over them [was] Zabdiel son of Haggedolim.

en.L: and their brothers, mighty men of strength: 128; and overseer over them [was] Zabdiel son of Haggedolim.
en.B: and their fellow priests, capable men, 128 in all. Their overseer was Zabdiel son of Haggedolim.
en.R: and their fellow priests, strong and able men, 128 in all. Zabdiel son of Haggedolim was in charge of them.

decisions.choice: mighty men of strength: capable, able men
decisions.reason: The phrase often means warriors, but here it describes priests, so it means men of ability and standing (1 Chronicles 9:13 uses the same words of the priests, able men for the service of the house of God).

decisions.choice: Haggedolim: a name, "the great ones"
alternatives: son of one of the great men
decisions.reason: The word has the article and means "the great ones". It may be a family name, or it may say that Zabdiel was the son of one of the leading men. With the numbers of verses 12-14, the priests in the city number 1,192.

source.text: וּמִֽן־הַלְוִיִּ֑ם שְׁמַעְיָ֧ה בֶן־חַשּׁ֛וּב בֶּן־עַזְרִיקָ֥ם בֶּן־חֲשַׁבְיָ֖ה בֶּן־בּוּנִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And of the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, son of Bunni;

en.L: And of the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, son of Bunni;
en.B: From the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, son of Bunni;
en.R: From the Levites there was Shemaiah son of Hasshub, the son of Azrikam, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Bunni.

decisions.choice: Shemaiah son of Hasshub: also in 1 Chronicles 9:14
decisions.reason: 1 Chronicles 9:14 names him first among the Levites of Jerusalem, of the descendants of Merari.

source.text: וְשַׁבְּתַ֨י וְיוֹזָבָ֜ד עַל־הַמְּלָאכָ֤ה הַחִֽיצֹנָה֙ לְבֵ֣ית הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים מֵרָאשֵׁ֖י הַלְוִיִּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and Shabbethai and Jozabad, over the work, the outside [work], of [the] house of God, of [the] heads of the Levites;

en.L: and Shabbethai and Jozabad, of the heads of the Levites, [were] over the outside work of the house of God;
en.B: and Shabbethai and Jozabad, leaders of the Levites, who were in charge of the outside work of the house of God;
en.R: Shabbethai and Jozabad were leaders of the Levites. They were in charge of the work outside the temple.

decisions.choice: the outside work: duties outside the temple itself
decisions.reason: The outside work is the business of the temple apart from the worship inside it: supplies, buildings and the like. 1 Chronicles 26:29 uses the same expression for Levites who served as officers and judges.

decisions.choice: Shabbethai and Jozabad: Levites who helped Ezra
decisions.reason: A Levite Jozabad weighed the temple treasure Ezra brought (Ezra 8:33), and both names are among the Levites who explained the law (8:7).

decisions.choice: of the heads of the Levites placed after the names
decisions.reason: Literal moves this phrase from the end of the verse to stand next to the names it describes, so the sentence can be read.

source.text: וּמַתַּנְיָ֣ה בֶן־מִ֠יכָה בֶּן־זַבְדִּ֨י בֶן־אָסָ֜ף רֹ֗אשׁ הַתְּחִלָּה֙ יְהוֹדֶ֣ה לַתְּפִלָּ֔ה וּבַקְבֻּקְיָ֖ה מִשְׁנֶ֣ה מֵאֶחָ֑יו וְעַבְדָּא֙ בֶּן־שַׁמּ֔וּעַ בֶּן־גָּלָ֖ל בֶּן־יְדוּתֽוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: and Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zabdi, son of Asaph, [the] head of the beginning, he gave thanks for the prayer, and Bakbukiah, second of his brothers, and Abda son of Shammua, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun.

en.L: and Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zabdi, son of Asaph, the leader of the beginning, [who] gave thanks at prayer, and Bakbukiah, the second among his brothers, and Abda son of Shammua, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun.
en.B: and Mattaniah son of Mica, son of Zabdi, son of Asaph, the leader who began the thanksgiving at prayer; Bakbukiah, second among his fellow Levites; and Abda son of Shammua, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun.
en.R: Mattaniah son of Mica, the son of Zabdi, the son of Asaph, was the leader who started the songs of thanks at prayer time. Bakbukiah was next to him among the Levites. There was also Abda son of Shammua, the son of Galal, the son of Jeduthun.

decisions.choice: the leader of the beginning: the one who began the thanksgiving
decisions.reason: The phrase is unusual. As it stands it means the one who led off, starting the thanksgiving in worship. With one letter different it would read "the leader of the praise", the head of the singers. Either way Mattaniah led the temple song (12:8).

decisions.choice: Asaph and Jeduthun: two of the families of singers appointed in David's time
decisions.reason: David appointed the sons of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun to lead the music of worship (1 Chronicles 25:1). Their descendants still served as singers after the exile.

decisions.choice: Jeduthun: the name as the Hebrew text is read
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the Hebrew text spell Jedithun; the scribes' note in the margin gives the usual form Jeduthun, which the vowels follow.

decisions.choice: his fellow Levites (Balanced); among the Levites (Readable)
decisions.reason: The brothers are the other Levites; Literal keeps "his brothers". Readable says "songs of thanks", since the thanksgiving was sung.

source.text: כָּל־הַלְוִיִּם֙ בְּעִ֣יר הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ מָאתַ֖יִם שְׁמֹנִ֥ים וְאַרְבָּעָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: All the Levites in the city of the holiness: two hundred eighty and four.

en.L: All the Levites in the holy city: 284.
en.B: All the Levites in the holy city were 284.
en.R: In all, there were 284 Levites in the holy city.

decisions.choice: the holy city: Jerusalem
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, Jerusalem is called the holy city because God's house is there.

source.text: וְהַשּֽׁוֹעֲרִים֙ עַקּ֣וּב טַלְמ֔וֹן וַאֲחֵיהֶ֖ם הַשֹּׁמְרִ֣ים בַּשְּׁעָרִ֑ים מֵאָ֖ה שִׁבְעִ֥ים וּשְׁנָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And the gatekeepers: Akkub, Talmon and their brothers, the [ones] keeping [watch] at the gates: one hundred seventy and two.

en.L: And the gatekeepers: Akkub, Talmon and their brothers, who kept [watch] at the gates: 172.
en.B: The gatekeepers: Akkub, Talmon and their fellow gatekeepers, who kept watch at the gates, 172 in all.
en.R: The gatekeepers were Akkub, Talmon and their relatives, who guarded the gates. There were 172 of them.

decisions.choice: the gatekeepers: those who guarded the temple gates
decisions.reason: Akkub and Talmon were families of gatekeepers from the first return (7:45; Ezra 2:42; 1 Chronicles 9:17). They guarded the gates of the temple and its storerooms (12:25).

decisions.choice: their brothers (Literal); their fellow gatekeepers (Balanced); their relatives (Readable)
decisions.reason: The "brothers" are the others of the same families and duty.

source.text: וּשְׁאָ֨ר יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל הַכֹּהֲנִ֤ים הַלְוִיִּם֙ בְּכָל־עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה אִ֖ישׁ בְּנַחֲלָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] rest of Israel, the priests, the Levites, [were] in all [the] cities of Judah, each in his inheritance.

en.L: And the rest of Israel, the priests, the Levites, [were] in all the towns of Judah, each on his inheritance.
en.B: The rest of the Israelites, priests and Levites were in all the towns of Judah, every family on its own inherited land.
en.R: The rest of the Israelites, priests and Levites lived in all the other towns of Judah, each family on its own land.

decisions.choice: the rest of Israel: picking up what verse 3 said in passing
decisions.reason: After the list of Jerusalem's residents, the text returns to those who stayed in the towns (verse 3). The towns are named in verses 25-36.

decisions.choice: his inheritance: the family's inherited land
decisions.reason: The word means land handed down within a family, which the law kept in the family (Numbers 27:8-11; 1 Kings 21:3).

decisions.choice: every family on its own inherited land
decisions.reason: The land was held by families, so Balanced and Readable say "every family"; Literal keeps "each on his inheritance".

source.text: וְהַנְּתִינִ֖ים יֹשְׁבִ֣ים בָּעֹ֑פֶל וְצִיחָ֥א וְגִשְׁפָּ֖א עַל־הַנְּתִינִֽים׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And the Nethinim [were] dwelling on the Ophel, and Ziha and Gishpa [were] over the Nethinim.

en.L: And the Nethinim were living on the Ophel, and Ziha and Gishpa [were] over the Nethinim.
en.B: The temple servants lived on the Ophel, and Ziha and Gishpa were in charge of the temple servants.
en.R: The temple servants lived on the hill called Ophel, next to the temple. Ziha and Gishpa were in charge of them.

decisions.choice: the Ophel: the hill between the temple and the old City of David
decisions.reason: The temple servants lived on the Ophel near the temple, where they worked (3:26-27). Ziha was the name of a family of temple servants from the first return (7:46; Ezra 2:43).

decisions.choice: the Nethinim (Literal); the temple servants (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The project's wording for this group. Readable adds "the hill called" and "next to the temple" so the reader can place it.

source.text: וּפְקִ֤יד הַלְוִיִּם֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם עֻזִּ֤י בֶן־בָּנִי֙ בֶּן־חֲשַׁבְיָ֔ה בֶּן־מַתַּנְיָ֖ה בֶּן־מִיכָ֑א מִבְּנֵ֤י אָסָף֙ הַמְשֹׁ֣רְרִ֔ים לְנֶ֖גֶד מְלֶ֥אכֶת בֵּית־הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem [was] Uzzi son of Bani, son of Hashabiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Mica, of [the] sons of Asaph, the singers, in front of [the] work of [the] house of God.

en.L: And the overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem [was] Uzzi son of Bani, son of Hashabiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Mica, of the sons of Asaph, the singers, over the work of the house of God.
en.B: The overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi son of Bani, son of Hashabiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Mica, one of the descendants of Asaph, the singers who were responsible for the service of the house of God.
en.R: The overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem was Uzzi son of Bani, the son of Hashabiah, the son of Mattaniah, the son of Mica. He was from the family of Asaph, the singers who were in charge of the music in the temple of God.

decisions.choice: the singers, over the work of the house of God: the singers' charge, or Uzzi's
alternatives: Uzzi was over the work of the house of God
decisions.reason: The phrase may describe the singers, who were responsible for the music of the temple's worship, or it may go back to Uzzi as overseer. The meaning is close either way.

decisions.choice: Mattaniah son of Mica: the singer of verse 17
decisions.reason: Uzzi is the great-grandson of the Mattaniah named in verse 17. The list may join families of more than one generation, or Uzzi may have held the office at a later time.

source.text: כִּֽי־מִצְוַ֥ת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וַאֲמָנָ֥ה עַל־הַמְשֹׁרְרִ֖ים דְּבַר־י֥וֹם בְּיוֹמֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: For [the] commandment of the king [was] on them, and a fixed arrangement on the singers, [the] matter of a day in its day.

en.L: For the commandment of the king [was] on them, and a fixed arrangement [was] on the singers, the matter of a day in its day.
en.B: For there was a command from the king concerning them, and a fixed arrangement for the singers, providing what each day required.
en.R: The king had given orders about the singers, and there was a set rule for what they would receive each day.

decisions.choice: the king: probably the Persian king, perhaps David
alternatives: King David, who organized the singers
decisions.reason: Verse 24 speaks of the Persian king, and Persian kings did grant support to the temple's servants (Ezra 7:24). But David's command about the singers is mentioned in 12:24 and 12:45-46, and "the king" could mean him. The text does not say.

decisions.choice: a fixed arrangement, the matter of a day in its day: a settled daily provision
alternatives: a fixed schedule of duties for each day
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the people's pledge in 10:1, something fixed and binding. "The matter of a day in its day" means what each day required, the phrase used for the daily portions of the singers in 12:47. It may refer to their food and support, or to the order of their daily duties.

decisions.choice: what they would receive each day
decisions.reason: Readable follows the more likely reading, the daily provision; the decision above gives the other.

source.text: וּפְתַֽחְיָ֨ה בֶּן־מְשֵֽׁיזַבְאֵ֜ל מִבְּנֵי־זֶ֤רַח בֶּן־יְהוּדָה֙ לְיַ֣ד הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְכָל־דָּבָ֖ר לָעָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, of [the] sons of Zerah son of Judah, [was] at [the] hand of the king for every matter of the people.

en.L: And Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, of the sons of Zerah son of Judah, [was] at the king's hand for every matter of the people.
en.B: Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, a descendant of Zerah son of Judah, was the king's agent in every matter concerning the people.
en.R: Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, from the family of Zerah son of Judah, acted for the king in everything that concerned the people.

decisions.choice: at the king's hand: acting as the king's agent
alternatives: the king's adviser at the Persian court
decisions.reason: To be at someone's hand is to serve as his agent. Pethahiah may have represented the Persian king in Judah in matters affecting the people, or represented the people at the king's court. The text does not say where he served.

decisions.choice: Zerah son of Judah: the second of Judah's great clans
decisions.reason: Zerah was the twin brother of Perez (Genesis 38:29-30). With Perez (verse 4) he heads one of the clans of Judah (Numbers 26:20).

source.text: וְאֶל־הַחֲצֵרִ֖ים בִּשְׂדֹתָ֑ם מִבְּנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֗ה יָֽשְׁב֞וּ בְּקִרְיַ֤ת הָֽאַרְבַּע֙ וּבְנֹתֶ֔יהָ וּבְדִיבֹן֙ וּבְנֹתֶ֔יהָ וּבִֽיקַּבְצְאֵ֖ל וַחֲצֵרֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And to the villages with their fields: [some] of [the] sons of Judah dwelt in Kiriath-arba and its daughters, and in Dibon and its daughters, and in Jekabzeel and its villages,

en.L: And as for the villages with their fields, some of the sons of Judah lived in Kiriath-arba and its daughters, and in Dibon and its daughters, and in Jekabzeel and its villages,
en.B: As for the villages with their fields, some of the descendants of Judah lived in Kiriath-arba and its surrounding towns, in Dibon and its surrounding towns, in Jekabzeel and its villages,
en.R: Some of the descendants of Judah lived in villages with their fields around them: in Kiriath-arba and the towns around it, in Dibon and the towns around it, in Jekabzeel and its villages,

decisions.choice: Kiriath-arba: the old name of Hebron
decisions.reason: Kiriath-arba is Hebron (Genesis 23:2; Joshua 14:15), the chief town of the hill country of Judah. The list uses the old names of several towns.

decisions.choice: the villages with their fields: the start of a list of towns outside Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Verses 25-30 name the places where people of Judah lived, and verses 31-35 those of Benjamin. Many of Judah's towns lie in the far south of Judah's old land (Joshua 15:21-36), beyond what the province of Judah seems to have held at this time, so the list may show where families had their old homes and land.

decisions.choice: its daughters: the smaller settlements around a town
decisions.reason: A town's "daughters" are the villages that depended on it, as children on a mother (Numbers 21:25; Joshua 15:45). They are distinct from the open "villages" (verses 25, 30), which had no walls.

decisions.choice: its surrounding towns (Balanced); the towns around it (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture "its daughters"; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

source.text: וּבְיֵשׁ֥וּעַ וּבְמוֹלָדָ֖ה וּבְבֵ֥ית פָּֽלֶט׃

records.literal_gloss: and in Jeshua and in Moladah and in Beth-pelet,

en.L: and in Jeshua and in Moladah and in Beth-pelet,
en.B: in Jeshua, Moladah, Beth-pelet,
en.R: in Jeshua, Moladah, Beth-pelet,

decisions.choice: Moladah, Beth-pelet: towns in the south of Judah
decisions.reason: Both are among the towns of the Negev in Judah's allotment (Joshua 15:26-27). Jeshua is named only here.

decisions.choice: the repeated "and in" left out
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "and in" before each town; Balanced and Readable list the towns as English does, and Literal keeps the repetition.

source.text: וּבַחֲצַ֥ר שׁוּעָ֛ל וּבִבְאֵ֥ר שֶׁ֖בַע וּבְנֹתֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: and in Hazar-shual and in Beersheba and its daughters,

en.L: and in Hazar-shual and in Beersheba and its daughters,
en.B: Hazar-shual, Beersheba and its surrounding towns,
en.R: Hazar-shual, Beersheba and the towns around it,

decisions.choice: Beersheba: the southern limit of the land
decisions.reason: Beersheba lay at the southern edge of the settled land, so that "from Dan to Beersheba" meant the whole land (Judges 20:1). Hazar-shual is near it (Joshua 15:28).

decisions.choice: its daughters: the smaller settlements around a town
decisions.reason: A town's "daughters" are the villages that depended on it, as children on a mother (Numbers 21:25; Joshua 15:45). They are distinct from the open "villages" (verses 25, 30), which had no walls.

decisions.choice: its surrounding towns (Balanced); the towns around it (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture "its daughters"; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

source.text: וּבְצִֽקְלַ֥ג וּבִמְכֹנָ֖ה וּבִבְנֹתֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: and in Ziklag and in Meconah and in its daughters,

en.L: and in Ziklag and in Meconah and in its daughters,
en.B: Ziklag, Meconah and its surrounding towns,
en.R: Ziklag, Meconah and the towns around it,

decisions.choice: Ziklag: the town David held before he was king
decisions.reason: The Philistine king Achish gave Ziklag to David (1 Samuel 27:6). It lay in the far south (Joshua 15:31). Meconah is named only here.

decisions.choice: its daughters: the smaller settlements around a town
decisions.reason: A town's "daughters" are the villages that depended on it, as children on a mother (Numbers 21:25; Joshua 15:45). They are distinct from the open "villages" (verses 25, 30), which had no walls.

decisions.choice: its surrounding towns (Balanced); the towns around it (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture "its daughters"; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

source.text: וּבְעֵ֥ין רִמּ֛וֹן וּבְצָרְעָ֖ה וּבְיַרְמֽוּת׃

records.literal_gloss: and in En-rimmon and in Zorah and in Jarmuth,

en.L: and in En-rimmon and in Zorah and in Jarmuth,
en.B: En-rimmon, Zorah, Jarmuth,
en.R: En-rimmon, Zorah, Jarmuth,

decisions.choice: Zorah, Jarmuth: towns of the western foothills
decisions.reason: Zorah, Samson's home town (Judges 13:2), and Jarmuth lay in the low hills west of Judah's highlands (Joshua 15:33-35). En-rimmon was in the south (Joshua 15:32, where it may be written as two names, Ain and Rimmon).

decisions.choice: the repeated "and in" left out
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "and in" before each town; Balanced and Readable list the towns as English does, and Literal keeps the repetition.

source.text: זָנֹ֤חַ עֲדֻלָּם֙ וְחַצְרֵיהֶ֔ם לָכִישׁ֙ וּשְׂדֹתֶ֔יהָ עֲזֵקָ֖ה וּבְנֹתֶ֑יהָ וַיַּחֲנ֥וּ מִבְּאֵֽר־שֶׁ֖בַע עַד־גֵּֽיא־הִנֹּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Zanoah, Adullam and their villages, Lachish and its fields, Azekah and its daughters; and they encamped from Beersheba to [the] valley of Hinnom.

en.L: Zanoah, Adullam and their villages, Lachish and its fields, Azekah and its daughters; and they encamped from Beersheba to the valley of Hinnom.
en.B: Zanoah, Adullam and their villages, Lachish and its fields, and Azekah and its surrounding towns. So they settled from Beersheba to the valley of Hinnom.
en.R: Zanoah, Adullam and their villages, Lachish and its fields, and Azekah and the towns around it. So the people of Judah settled all the way from Beersheba in the south to the valley of Hinnom by Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Lachish, Azekah: fortified towns of the foothills
decisions.reason: Lachish and Azekah were among the last cities of Judah to hold out against Babylon (Jeremiah 34:7). Zanoah and Adullam are in the same region (Joshua 15:34-35).

decisions.choice: encamped: settled, perhaps in a temporary way
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to pitch camp. Here it means that they made their homes over this whole area; it may suggest that the settlements were still small and not fully rebuilt.

decisions.choice: from Beersheba to the valley of Hinnom: from the far south to the edge of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The valley of Hinnom runs along the south side of Jerusalem and marked the border between Judah and Benjamin (Joshua 15:8). Judah's settlements reached from there to Beersheba.

decisions.choice: its daughters: the smaller settlements around a town
decisions.reason: A town's "daughters" are the villages that depended on it, as children on a mother (Numbers 21:25; Joshua 15:45). They are distinct from the open "villages" (verses 25, 30), which had no walls.

decisions.choice: the people of Judah; in the south; by Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable names who settled and where the two places are, so the reader sees the span of the land.

source.text: וּבְנֵ֥י בִנְיָמִ֖ן מִגָּ֑בַע מִכְמָ֣שׂ וְעַיָּ֔ה וּבֵֽית־אֵ֖ל וּבְנֹתֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] sons of Benjamin from Geba: Micmash and Aija and Bethel and its daughters,

en.L: And the sons of Benjamin from Geba: Micmash and Aija and Bethel and its daughters,
en.B: The descendants of Benjamin lived from Geba onward, in Micmash, Aija, Bethel and its surrounding towns,
en.R: The descendants of Benjamin lived in the towns from Geba on: Micmash, Aija, Bethel and the towns around it,

decisions.choice: from Geba: from Geba onward, the starting point of Benjamin's towns
alternatives: those from Geba lived in Micmash ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is short: "the sons of Benjamin from Geba". It most likely means that Benjamin's people lived from Geba on, in the towns that follow. Geba was the northern limit of Judah in the time of the kings (2 Kings 23:8).

decisions.choice: Aija, Bethel: Ai and Bethel north of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Aija is a form of Ai, near Bethel (Joshua 7:2). Men of Bethel and Ai were among the returned exiles (7:32). Micmash too is near (1 Samuel 13:2).

decisions.choice: lived from Geba onward
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the verb from verse 25 and say how "from Geba" relates to the names that follow. Literal keeps the bare Hebrew.

decisions.choice: its daughters: the smaller settlements around a town
decisions.reason: A town's "daughters" are the villages that depended on it, as children on a mother (Numbers 21:25; Joshua 15:45). They are distinct from the open "villages" (verses 25, 30), which had no walls.

en.L: Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
en.B: Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
en.R: Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,

decisions.choice: Anathoth, Nob: towns of priests near Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Anathoth was Jeremiah's home town and a town of priests (Jeremiah 1:1). Nob, "the town of the priests", lay within sight of Jerusalem (1 Samuel 22:19; Isaiah 10:32).

decisions.choice: Hazor, Ramah: towns of Benjamin, not the Hazor of the north
decisions.reason: This Hazor is a small town of Benjamin, not the great city in Galilee (Joshua 11:10). Ramah is the town of Benjamin north of Jerusalem (Joshua 18:25).

decisions.choice: Hadid: a town near Lod
decisions.reason: Hadid is named with Lod and Ono in the list of returned exiles (7:37). Zeboim here is not the city destroyed with Sodom (Genesis 14:2).

en.L: Lod and Ono, Ge-harashim.
en.B: Lod and Ono, and Ge-harashim.
en.R: Lod and Ono, and the Valley of Craftsmen.

decisions.choice: Ge-harashim: "the valley of craftsmen"
decisions.reason: The name means "valley of craftsmen" (1 Chronicles 4:14). Lod and Ono lay in the plain toward the coast, where Nehemiah's enemies once asked him to meet them (6:2).

decisions.choice: the Valley of Craftsmen
decisions.reason: Readable translates the place name, as its meaning is known; Literal and Balanced keep the name.

records.literal_gloss: And of the Levites, divisions of Judah [were] to Benjamin.

en.L: And of the Levites, divisions of Judah [belonged] to Benjamin.
en.B: Some divisions of the Levites that had been in Judah were joined to Benjamin.
en.R: Some groups of Levites who had lived in Judah now lived with the people of Benjamin.

decisions.choice: divisions of Judah to Benjamin: some Levite groups of Judah settled in Benjamin
alternatives: some divisions of the Levites belonged to Judah and some to Benjamin
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is very brief. It most likely says that some divisions of Levites, counted with Judah, were settled among Benjamin. It could also mean that the Levites were shared between the two tribes' towns. The Levites had no land of their own and lived in towns among the other tribes (Numbers 35:2-8).
